findings.title: Journal entry body containing a NUL character causes 500 Internal Server Error
findings.expected: Entry saved or a 4xx with a clear reason
findings.actual: 500 Internal Server Error (plain text). SQLite length() stops at the NUL, so CHECK(length(body) BETWEEN 1 AND 500) fails and the IntegrityError is not handled. The same input on /api/tasks returns 201.

findings.title: Oversized plant_id / entry id causes 500 instead of 4xx
findings.steps: POST /api/journal with plant_id 99999999999999999999; GET /api/journal?plant_id=99999999999999999999; PUT or DELETE /api/journal/99999999999999999999
findings.actual: 500 Internal Server Error (SQLite integer overflow; ids have no upper bound)

findings.title: Journal requests have no timeout; a hung request leaves the page spinning or 'Saving…' forever
findings.steps: Make /api/journal requests hang (playwright route that delays 20s). Type a search on /journal, or click 'Add entry' on a plant page.
findings.expected: Fail after 10 s with a visible error and a working retry
findings.actual: After 13 s /journal still shows 'Loading entries…' with the previous query's results underneath. On the plant page, 'Add entry' still read 'Saving…' (disabled) after 12 s.
findings.evidence: innerText after 13 s: 'Loading entries… Tomato 2 Jul 2026 …'; submit button text 'Saving…' after 12 s

findings.title: Journal error states have no Retry button
findings.steps: Route /api/journal* to return 500/502, then open /journal (or type a search) or open a plant from /plants
findings.expected: Error message with a Retry action that reloads without a page reload
findings.actual: Only 'Could not load the journal.' is shown, with no retry. On the plant page the only way to recover is to reload or add an entry. On /journal you have to change the search text.
findings.evidence: Buttons on the page after the error: 'Sign out|Clear search' (journal); 'Sign out|Edit|Delete plant|Delete…|Add entry' (plant detail)

findings.title: Search longer than 80 characters shows a raw validation error
findings.steps: Type or paste 81+ characters into Search
findings.expected: Input limited to 80 (maxlength) or a friendly message
findings.actual: The page shows 'Query.q: String should have at most 80 characters' in place of results; the input has no maxlength
findings.evidence: Observed text 'Query.q: String should have at most 80 characters'

findings.title: Long unbroken plant name in the journal feed causes horizontal scrolling at 375 px
findings.steps: Create a plant named with 80 'W's, add a journal entry, open /journal at 375 px width
findings.expected: No sideways scrolling; the name wraps
findings.actual: document scrollWidth is 1568 px. .journal-feed is a CSS grid whose items keep min-width:auto, and the plant link has no overflow-wrap, so the whole card stretches.
findings.evidence: scrollWidth 1568 at 375 px with the long plant name; 375 once that plant was removed

findings.title: Search box is not synced with the URL; clicking 'Journal' in the nav while filtered keeps the old search
findings.steps: Open /journal?q=tom, click 'Journal' in the top navigation (or use browser back/forward)
findings.expected: Search cleared and all entries shown, matching the URL
findings.actual: The URL becomes /journal but the search box still says 'tom' and the page shows '3 entries match'

findings.title: Retried create after a timeout or lost response makes a duplicate entry; retried delete reports an error
findings.steps: Submit an entry whose response is lost (server saved it), then click 'Add entry' again; or delete when the response is lost and retry
findings.expected: One change; the retry is idempotent
findings.actual: POST has no idempotency key, so the retry inserts a second entry. A retried DELETE returns 404 'Journal entry not found.', which is shown as an error even though the entry is gone.
findings.evidence: Code: create_entry inserts unconditionally; delete_entry raises 404 when the entry is missing; the form keeps the text after an error, which invites a retry

findings.title: 'Future date' check uses server date vs browser date
findings.steps: Use the app from a timezone ahead of the server (e.g. UTC+12 while the server is UTC) and pick today's local date
findings.actual: The server validator uses date.today() in the server's timezone and rejects it with 'Journal date cannot be in the future.', while the form's max (browser-local today) allows it

findings.title: Character counter/maxlength counts UTF-16 units, so emoji entries are capped below 500 characters
findings.steps: Type 251+ emoji (e.g. 🌱) into the Entry textarea
findings.expected: 500 characters allowed (the server counts code points)
findings.actual: textarea maxlength=500 and the counter use String.length, so each emoji counts as 2 and input stops at 250 emoji
findings.evidence: The counter dropped by 7 for 'keep me' (correct) and by 14 for 'Edited text 😀' (the emoji counted as 2). The server accepted 500 'é' / combining sequences.
